target_customer: AI and machine learning teams (robotics, autonomous vehicles, medical imaging, enterprise) that need to label, curate and manage training data
problem: Teams building computer vision models spend large effort labeling and curating data with fragmented tools; Encord offers an annotation and data management platform with AI assisted labeling.
business_model: B2B SaaS and platform contracts for enterprise AI teams
product_category: Data labeling and data infrastructure for AI

founders.name: Eric Landau
founders.background_notes: Source: Encord YC company page. Other press snippets mention big data research in particle physics but those pages were not opened.

founders.name: Ulrik Stig Hansen
founders.background_notes: YC page gives title only. Press snippets mention J.P. Morgan and Imperial College London but those pages were not opened, so left null.

competitors.name: Labelbox
competitors.what: Training data platform for labeling and model development

competitors.name: Scale AI
competitors.what: Managed data labeling service with annotator workforce
competitors.funding_then: $325M Series E at $7.3B valuation in April 2021 (about one month after the batch)

competitors.name: Snorkel AI
competitors.funding_then: $85M raise in August 2021 at a $1B valuation (months after the batch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Annotation tooling for video and medical imaging plus model assisted labeling needs solid engineering and ML work, but the early product was a software platform rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: Customers store datasets and workflows in the platform, which creates switching costs, but several funded rivals sold similar tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying Encord; it stayed independent and raised through 2026.

market_need_then: Computer vision teams were scaling model development in 2020 and 2021, and data labeling vendors raised large rounds in early 2021 (Labelbox $40M, Scale $325M), showing funded demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and enterprise, per site copy

rebrands.why: No source explains the change; a YC link slug and press snippets show the earlier name Cord.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is short and distinctive, but no press or community evidence about the brand itself was found, and the rename from Cord is unexplained.

pivots.from: Computer vision data labeling and annotation platform
pivots.to: Data layer for physical AI (robotics, autonomous vehicles)
pivots.why: Positioning change visible between the 2024 TechCrunch description and the 2026 YC page and Series C announcement; the company's own reasoning was not read.

outcome_analysis: Encord launched its product during YC in spring 2021 and raised a seed in June 2021, a Series A in October 2021, a $30M Series B in 2024 and a $60M Series C in 2026, reaching about $110M total. The AI data boom and growing computer vision and robotics demand supported growth, and the company claims 300 plus enterprise teams as customers. Strong funded rivals existed, so differentiation through AI assisted tooling and later the physical AI focus mattered.
notes: Seed amount and date come from search summaries of aggregators and the Encord blog mirror (page shows a Nov 2022 publication date, so the June 2021 date is unverified). Series A amount conflicts: $15M in most outlets, $12.5M in one. A Feb 2021 pre seed of $500K led by YC is seen only in one snippet and is unverified. Series C valuation of $550M was reported in one search summary only; not recorded. CB Insights dates the Series C December 2025, other outlets and the company say February 2026. Series A source link is a TechCrunch page found by search, not opened. Company site fetch returned truncated content.
